julia: heads-up: saw thrash in kernel selection when we mix short (<=32) and long (>2048) requests in same batch on a100. allocator spikes & fallback to generic kernel.
omar: ugh, is this the prefill->decode path mismatch we've seen before?
julia: looks related. profiler shows hot path: choose_kernel_for_seqlength() flipping between fmha_fp16 and fallback_tf32 every other request.
kevin: can you paste the trace? stack or flamegraph?
julia: here's quick snippet from trace:
```
choose_kernel_for_seqlength(seq_len=28) -> kernel=fast_fmha
choose_kernel_for_seqlength(seq_len=2100) -> kernel=fallback_kv_split
choose_kernel_for_seqlength(seq_len=30) -> kernel=fast_fmha
```
kevin: hmm kernel selection is not sticky per-batch; we're re-evaluating per-request inside a continuous batch, causing kernel reinit overhead.
julia: also KV cache miss rate rose ~12% when mixed sequences hit the same GPU — eviction churn.
omar: could batching heuristic be coalescing incompatible sequences? maybe our bin classifier is too coarse.
kevin: suggestion: try gating on avg_seq_length per microbatch and force homogeneous sub-batches before kernel switch. A/B test: enable `--gating=avg_seq` and measure p99.
build-bot: CI perf job triggered: https://ci.redwood/18412/seq-bin-experiment :white_check_mark:
natalie: I'll run a replay with kv-ttl tuning and sticky-kernel flag, will post perf diffs. :thumbsup:
julia: thanks. if we can avoid kernel reinit (CUDA module loads) that's likely ~4-6ms saved per switch, p99 win.
kevin: also need to update autotune training to record sequence-length histograms by GPU, not global.
omar: assignable tasks? I'll take mod to batching classifier; @natalie do the replay; @kevin update autotune.
julia: SGTM. dropping a small repro (logs + request mix) to #eng-runtime/test-runs in 5m.
